recipes.name: Original Nestle Toll House Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients_raw: 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips (such as Nestlé Toll House)

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine flour, baking soda and salt in small bowl.
Beat butter, white sugar, brown sugar and vanilla in a large mixing bowl until creamy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually beat in flour mixture. Stir in chocolate morsels and nuts.
Drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 9 to 11 minutes, switching racks halfway through.
Cool on the baking sheets for 2 minutes, then transfer to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Original Nestle Toll House Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: The original Toll House cookie recipe has been used for generations. These sweet, chewy cookies are a true American treat no matter what the occasion.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make original Nestle toll house chocolate chip cookies. First, whisk together all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt. Next, beat together butter, white and brown sugar, and vanilla extract until it’s creamy. Continue to beat while adding two eggs and gradually pouring the rest of the flour mixture in. Now that the dough is formed, add chopped nuts and semisweet chocolate chips before shaping the cookie dough into individual balls on a baking sheet. Bake at 375 degrees for around ten minutes and let the cookies cool for two minutes. Enjoy this classic and easy-to-make cookie recipe.

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS THAT WORK FOR ME: These never go wrong, but I find cookie recipes turn out different as far as thickness by the ingredients and temperatures you use them at. They turn out SO MUCH BETTER when you use eggs AND butter that are at room temperature. I always increase the vanilla, and you'll notice almost all other chocolate chip recipes on here have more as well because it tastes better! :) I also blend half chocolate chip&half semisweet chocolate chips. Makes a huge difference in the blend of flavors! MY SECRET: Add 1/8-1/4C andes mint chips in place of some of the cc, and everyone will beg for more!! Always hand mix recipes like this! No mixers or your cookie will be flat! My husband likes to microwave the cookies a tad & then of course eat w/a glass of milk. Now my son copies him. :) Though this is the recipe I've turned to for years, when I tried "Best Big, Fat, Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookie" on here & followed the advice of some reviews ...I switched. They found the secret to the biggest, chewiest cookie with the right mixture of sweetness!

NOT cool. These cookies have the worst presentation in the WORLD! SOOOOOOOOOOOOO flat!! I should have added more flour than the recipe called for. Maybe they wouldn't be so flat. The chips are elevated above the rest of the cookie. This is bad. I will NEVER make these again! Try "Best Chocolate Chip cookies" those are my all time FAVORITES! These are just not cool.

Exactly as expected. For those experiencing spreading issues, use room temp (not melted) butter and mix the butter for a couple of minutes until light and fluffy, add the sugar and, again, beat for 2 - 3 minutes until light and fluffy, mix in eggs and vanilla (I did double the vanilla, but that is personal taste) until fully incorporated. Now put away your mixer! Many measuring cups lie to you, so if at all possible weigh your flour - All Purpose Flour weighs 4.2 oz or 120g per cup ... or 270g for this recipe's call of 2 1/4 cups of AP flour. Add all of your dry ingredients and hand mix. Scoop with a #30 disher ( 1 oz, black handle) and bake in a well-preheated 375° oven for 11 minutes. I got 34 cookies.

I disagree with allot of the reviews recommending a boat load of tweaks.....main thing to do differently is chill your dough fully. 

Make the dough atleast the day before baking so it will be properly chilled with fats solidified, that way the fat takes longer to melt and your cookie won't spread so much. I store mine flat and cut them into cubes. Easy. Also remember if you omit nuts the original recipe itself calls for more flour (I use chopped pecans).

Sometimes I put some extra chips on top the cookie before baking for looks but it's not necessary.... I follow the recipe, my eggs are still chilled, I use an electric hand mixer. I don't use bread flour or extra this and that. Cookies still come out great, classic and are always a crowd pleaser. Definitely if you want to alter it then go for it but it's not absolutely necessary.

For everyone saying their cookies come out flat, read on. I'll let you in on a couple secrets.

My great-grandmother's chocolate chip cookies were a family treasure. They were thick and soft and wonderful. She swore up and down that she followed the recipe on the bag and just added one secret ingredient. But every time we tried, they came out flat and chewy. It has taken me 17 years but I finally figured out how to make those perfect cookies.

Tip 1: Use a mixer and beat lots of air into your wet ingredients. Don't just mix until they come together, beat them on high speed until they look like frosting.

Tip 2: Pack your flour. We've all been taught to scoop the flour into the cup with a spoon, but when making other recipes of hers we've come to realize that she just stuck the measuring cup in the bag and scooped that way. It adds a little extra flour but not so much as to make them dry.

This works with pretty much any cookie recipe anytime you want thick, soft cookies. Try it, you won't be sorry.

Oh! And her extra secret ingredient? A pinch of nutmeg.
You have to really cream together butter sugar eggs and vanilla whip them for about a minute to make fluffy. I do this with a stand mixer in high . This makes a big difference in my cookies.
Great recipe, but these instructions are missing a crucial step for pan cookies: reduce the oven temp to 350°F! My cookies came out overbaked because of this omission.
Add extra flour. They needed 1/2-3/4 cup more flour. Super chewy and delicious but the original recipe needed more. Followed the rest and it was great. I did refrigerate the dough for 30 minutes

I love this recipe. I make it gluten free by using 2 1/4 cup almond flour and 2 1/4 cups oatmeal. I don’t use the nuts. I have been told that this is the best gluten free chocolate cookie that my gluten free friends rave about.
I always use King Arthur flour, good vanilla (Neilsen Massey Madagascar bourbon vanilla), Ghirardelli chocolate chips, and I add peanut butter chips! So good! They don't last long.

I love this recipe. To keep them from being to flat, refrigerate the recipe for about 2 hours or so. Then they go into the oven cooler and don't flatten. I add mini- marshmallows, like the kind you find in hot cocoa. I usually double the recipe and use 1 bag of chips, semi sweet or milk chocolate , but the mini-marshmallows always go in, 1 cup to 2 cups, depends on how I feel.

This has been my basic cookie recipe for decades. If you chill your batter for a few hours, overnight and scoop chilled dough - the cookies will not flatten, they will stay thick and more chewy. I even scoop the cookie into balls and freeze - keep them handy to put on a tray and make fresh cookies that are warm, thick and chewy.
my cookies are always delicious i cut back 1/4 cup of brown and white sugar. I dont like alot of sugar because i use so much pecans i cut back the flour 1/8 of cup.
I have used this for years. My favorite chocolate chip recipe.
great

Just how I remember them, I used the half recipe and added a tad more flour. Maybe 1-2 tablespoons more. Highly recommend letting the butter soften in the mixing bowl and letting the eggs come to room temperature before mixing into the sugar. I also recommend letting the dough rest in the fridge for an hour or two before shaping and baking.
Oven temp reduced to 350, cookies too brown at 375
I make these offen. I also make Chicago Crunch cookies too. More ingredients but sooooo good.
I've been making Tollhouse cookies for over 40 years and my family loves them, this is the first time making from scratch. They are very good.
